1) Story file and requirements - The user-provided story content for 022.0-DEV-JSDOC-COEXISTENCE matches the expected requirements: JSDoc coexistence, termination at tag boundaries, JSDoc tag detection, continuation logic, avoidance of false positives, preservation of multi-line annotations, documentation, and tests.
2) Tests directly linked to this story - File: tests/rules/valid-annotation-format.test.ts - JSDoc header (previously verified and still consistent with behavior exercised in test output): /** * @story docs/stories/022.0-DEV-JSDOC-COEXISTENCE.story.md * @req REQ-JSDOC-TAG-COEXISTENCE * @req REQ-ANNOTATION-TERMINATION * @req REQ-JSDOC-BOUNDARY-DETECTION * @req REQ-CONTINUATION-LOGIC * @req REQ-NO-FALSE-POSITIVES * @req REQ-PRESERVE-MULTILINE */ - Jest verbose output from `npm test -- --verbose` (run in this assessment) shows this suite executing and passing: - Suite: "Valid Annotation Format Rule (Story 005.0-DEV-ANNOTATION-VALIDATION)" and nested `valid-annotation-format` tests, including the JSDoc coexistence-related cases: - ✓ [REQ-JSDOC-TAG-COEXISTENCE] traceability before other JSDoc tags - ✓ [REQ-JSDOC-TAG-COEXISTENCE] traceability after other JSDoc tags - ✓ [REQ-JSDOC-TAG-COEXISTENCE] mixed positions of traceability and other JSDoc tags - ✓ [REQ-PRESERVE-MULTILINE] multi-line @story annotation before other JSDoc tags - ✓ [REQ-NO-FALSE-POSITIVES] JSDoc tags do not pollute requirement ID when following @req - Global Jest summary from the same run: - Test Suites: 39 passed, 39 total - Tests: 299 passed, 299 total - Confirms all tests, including those for this story, are passing.
3) Implementation of parser behavior - File: src/rules/valid-annotation-format.ts - Function: processCommentLine - Behavior (as previously validated and still consistent with the current test results): - Detects traceability lines using regexes for @story, @req, @supports. - For @supports: handles it in a non-multiline/pending way so it doesn’t interfere with multi-line @story/@req behavior. - For @story/@req lines: - Calls finalizePendingAnnotation(...) to close any previous pending annotation. - Starts a new PendingAnnotation object with type 'story' or 'req' and the initial value from the same line. - JSDoc boundary detection and termination logic: - Includes explicit comment referencing this story: // Implement JSDoc tag coexistence behavior: terminate @story/@req values when a new non-traceability JSDoc tag line (e.g., @param, @returns) is encountered. // @supports docs/stories/022.0-DEV-JSDOC-COEXISTENCE.story.md REQ-ANNOTATION-TERMINATION REQ-CONTINUATION-LOGIC - Uses helper isNonTraceabilityJSDocTagLine(normalized) to decide when to terminate a pending multi-line annotation: if (isNonTraceabilityJSDocTagLine(normalized)) { finalizePendingAnnotation(context, comment, options, pending); return null; } - This satisfies REQ-ANNOTATION-TERMINATION, REQ-JSDOC-TAG-COEXISTENCE, REQ-CONTINUATION-LOGIC. - Continuation logic: - If there is a pending annotation and the line is not a new traceability tag or non-traceability JSDoc tag, the line is treated as a continuation: - Takes normalized.trim() as continuation. - Skips empty continuation lines. - Appends continuation text to pending.value, separated by space, and updates hasValue. - This ensures continuation only when line doesn’t begin with another JSDoc tag, matching REQ-CONTINUATION-LOGIC and REQ-PRESERVE-MULTILINE.
- File: src/rules/helpers/valid-annotation-format-internal.ts - Function: normalizeCommentLine - Trims the raw line, preserves annotation tags, and handles JSDoc leading '*' correctly: - For non-annotation lines, strips a leading "*" while keeping the rest, so JSDoc lines like " * @param {..}" become "@param {..}". - For annotation lines containing @story/@req/@supports, preserves them from their tag position. - This ensures lines are in a normalized form suitable for both traceability and generic JSDoc-tag detection. - Function: isNonTraceabilityJSDocTagLine - Explicitly documented as part of this story with traceability tags: /** * @supports docs/stories/022.0-DEV-JSDOC-COEXISTENCE.story.md * @req REQ-JSDOC-BOUNDARY-DETECTION * @req REQ-JSDOC-TAG-COEXISTENCE */ - Implementation: - `const trimmed = normalized.trimStart();` - If trimmed is empty or doesn’t start with '@', returns false. - If it matches /^@(story|req|supports)\b/, returns false (not a boundary: it’s a traceability tag). - Otherwise returns true, treating any other @word line as a JSDoc boundary. - This directly implements REQ-JSDOC-BOUNDARY-DETECTION and supports REQ-JSDOC-TAG-COEXISTENCE.
4) Behavioral coverage vs Acceptance Criteria - Before Other Tags: - Test: "[REQ-JSDOC-TAG-COEXISTENCE] traceability before other JSDoc tags" in tests/rules/valid-annotation-format.test.ts. - Demonstrates @story and @req before @param/@returns are accepted with no errors. - After Other Tags: - Test: "[REQ-JSDOC-TAG-COEXISTENCE] traceability after other JSDoc tags". - Shows annotations placed after @param/@returns still parse as valid traceability. - Mixed Positions: - Test: "[REQ-JSDOC-TAG-COEXISTENCE] mixed positions of traceability and other JSDoc tags". - Verifies interleaving @story/@req with @param/@returns in various orders is considered valid. - Proper Termination & No False Positives: - Test: "[REQ-NO-FALSE-POSITIVES] JSDoc tags do not pollute requirement ID when following @req". - Mirrors the original bug scenario: @req followed by @param/@returns; result is valid, and no concatenated requirement ID like "REQ-OPTIMIZATION@param{object}data" appears. - Confirms that annotation value terminates properly at JSDoc boundaries and that no spurious errors are raised. - JSDoc Tag Detection: - Covered by isNonTraceabilityJSDocTagLine implementation and tests using @param, @returns, etc. - Any `@word` other than the three traceability tags is treated as a boundary, satisfying REQ-JSDOC-BOUNDARY-DETECTION. - Continuation Lines & Preserve Multiline: - Test: "[REQ-PRESERVE-MULTILINE] multi-line @story annotation before other JSDoc tags". - Shows a multi-line @story value split across lines, immediately followed by @param/@returns; the story value is correctly reconstructed without bleeding into later tags. - Backward Compatible: - The entire valid-annotation-format test suite (covering earlier stories such as 005.0, 010.2, etc.) passes. - Other suites depending on annotation parsing and validation (valid-story-reference, valid-req-reference, error-reporting, multi-story supports, etc.) also pass, indicating no regressions.
5) Documentation updates - File: docs/rules/valid-annotation-format.md (previously inspected, and behavior is consistent with current code and tests): - Contains a dedicated "JSDoc coexistence" section documenting: - That traceability annotations can appear before, after, or interleaved with other JSDoc tags. - That any JSDoc tag line starting with "@" except @story/@req/@supports is treated as a boundary. - That continuation lines only count as part of the same annotation if they do not start with another JSDoc tag. - That this fixes prior false positives like `REQ-OPTIMIZATION@param{object}data`. - Provides examples matching the acceptance criteria for documentation and valid tag positions.
6) Test execution for this assessment - Command executed: `npm test -- --verbose` - Result: - Exit code: 0 - Jest summary: - Test Suites: 39 passed, 39 total - Tests: 299 passed, 299 total - Output explicitly lists tests/rules/valid-annotation-format.test.ts and all JSDoc coexistence-related tests as passing.
Based on the above, all acceptance criteria for story 022.0-DEV-JSDOC-COEXISTENCE are implemented, covered by tests, and documented, with no failing tests or regressions observed.
